lines.en: December 31st, Thursday. Clear, with frost. Breakfast at seven. We ate at the inn in Kameyama and walked to Seki.

lines.en: Today's entry is a little stiff. The town of Seki makes me write this way.

lines.en: From the east fork to the west fork, nearly two hundred old houses run on without a break.

lines.kana: しゅくばのなごりをこれほどのこしたまちを、わたしはまだしらない。
lines.en: I have yet to see another town that has kept so much of what a post town was.

lines.en: Frost covered the roof tiles white, and no shop curtains were out yet. The town on the morning of New Year's Eve was every bit as quiet as it should be.

lines.en: Tiles, white walls, latticed windows. Not decoration for tourists; the place has the air of somewhere people still live.

lines.en: They say this was once an especially prosperous post town, even for the Tōkaidō: the road to Ise begins at the east fork.

lines.kana: にひゃくねんのおもかげをのこすとおりは、あるくひとにむかしをかんじさせずにはおかない。
lines.en: A street that keeps the look of two hundred years ago cannot fail to make anyone walking it feel the past.

lines.en: We went into a hatago inn that has been kept as a museum. Upstairs, an old wooden board hung on the wall.

lines.en: "Horses must not be tied here. No loud talk at night. Do not go to bed with a fire still burning."

lines.en: The letters had faded; those three were all I could read. Travelers two hundred years ago were scolded just as I am.

lines.ja: {日記|にっき}の{下|した}に、{自分|じぶん}のための{規則|きそく}を{一|ひと}つ{書|か}き{加|くわ}えた。「{旅|たび}の{終|お}わりを{急|いそ}ぐべからず」。
lines.kana: にっきのしたに、じぶんのためのきそくをひとつかきくわえた。「たびのおわりをいそぐべからず」。
lines.en: At the bottom of the page I added one rule for myself: "Do not hurry the end of the journey."

lines.en: Past three in the afternoon the sun was already nearing the Suzuka mountains, and the shadows of the low roofs stretched until they all but touched the walls of the houses opposite.

lines.en: Winter days are short. Almost before the shadows touched the walls, the town turned the color of evening.

lines.kana: きょうのやどは、まついさんのふるいいえである。かめやまのなかじまさんのしょうかいというえんであった。
lines.en: Tonight's lodging is Matsui-san's old house, a connection that came through Nakajima-san in Kameyama.

lines.en: In the kitchen, Matsui-san and her mother had begun the New Year's cooking. Ken had hardly peered in before he was holding a knife.

lines.kana: かりただいどころが、またひとつふえた。だいどころをかりたいじょう、さらをあらわずにはすまない。ケンはよろこんであらう。
lines.en: One more borrowed kitchen. Having borrowed it, he cannot get away without washing the dishes; Ken washes them gladly.

lines.en: A sweet smell drifted from the pot of simmering beans, and the scent of dashi layered over it. Her mother's work was meticulous, and wasted nothing.

lines.en: Rolling the omelets became Ken's job. As fast as he rolled them, her mother silently fixed their shape. By the third, she stopped fixing them.

lines.kana: たなかさんをむかえるべく、くじはんにえきへむかった。ことしのしゅうでんはくじよんじゅうにふん。たなかさんはえきをでるなり、とけいをみてまんぞくそうにうなずいた。
lines.en: We headed to the station at half past nine to meet Tanaka-san; the year's last train was the 9:42. The moment he stepped out of the station he looked at his watch and nodded, satisfied.

lines.en: The clock on the inn's pillar was a minute slow. Tanaka-san said the clock was at fault. As always.

lines.ja: {夜|よる}、{大晦日|おおみそか}のそばを{皆|みな}で{食|た}べた。{三人|さんにん}の{客|きゃく}のそばまで、お{母|かあ}さんは{当|あ}たり{前|まえ}のように{用意|ようい}していた。

lines.en: That night we all ate the New Year's Eve soba. Her mother had prepared it for the three guests too, as if that were only natural.

lines.en: Just before midnight the three of us walked to Jizō-in. Our breath was white, the stars flickered, and the street had people in it again.

lines.en: No sooner had the bell begun than the line fell silent. With each stroke the reverberation receded over the town, and in the instant it died a new one laid itself over it.

lines.en: Tanaka-san bought one votive tablet and, without a word, wrote in his neat hand: "To finish walking." That was all. Not who, not where.

lines.en: Across forty years, from tomorrow Tanaka-san walks from here: the rest of the road that stopped at Ishiyakushi. Standing before the tablet, his back looked straighter than usual.

lines.en: I wrote nothing on a tablet. What I need to write, I can write in the diary.

lines.en: January 1st, Friday. Clear. Breakfast at half past eight. Late. But today of all days, no complaining.

lines.en: We ate the New Year's dishes from one box with Matsui-san's family. Ken's rolled omelets were, on the whole, straight.

lines.en: Sharing the first breakfast of the year with three strangers; there are people who do that as if it were nothing. I added one tick to the small kindnesses.

lines.en: Seki's one dish is not from a shop: it is this house's zōni, with one grilled rice cake in it.

lines.en: Before breakfast, at seven, the three of us stood in the street. The first sunrise appeared over toward the east fork, and the light poured into the single street like water.

lines.en: Tanaka-san did not look at his watch.

items.recapEn: They saw the year out in Seki, two hundred old houses under frost. Hana's diary turned literary: an inn's board of prohibitions, roof shadows reaching for the house opposite. Ken rolled omelets beside Matsui-san's mother; Tanaka-san came on the last train and at midnight wrote 'to finish walking' on a tablet. At dawn he never checked his watch.

items.recapEn: Waiting for the New Year's Eve bell at Jizō-in, Ken teased Hana about her literary diary. Tanaka-san returned from writing 'to finish walking' on a tablet and forecast a cloudy New Year's Day under a starry sky. Ken and Hana traded resolutions: Kyoto; one dish a day. From tomorrow he walks with them. Ken's pack, he claims, got lighter.
